Reason for Mistake: The Planner made a critical factual error by incorrectly associating the "over 60 million casualties" threshold with World War I. While the WebSurfer correctly identified that the Livesey Hall War Memorial commemorates both World War I and World War II, the Planner failed to verify the casualty figures for each war. Historically, World War I had approximately 20 million casualties, whereas World War II had over 60 million (approx. 70-85 million depending on the definition). By asserting that World War I is the war with over 60 million casualties, the Planner contradicted established historical facts and prematurely concluded the task with the wrong answer (World War I) instead of the correct one (World War II).
